result.title: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can leverage semantic feature names alongside summary statistics for tabular feature selection, yet it remains unclear when such information improves subset selection relative to established statistical methods. We investigate this question within an 18-dataset framework comprising 10 datasets for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training, 2 for checkpoint validation, and 6 held-out evaluation datasets. We compare five classical baselines, frozen Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.3-70B selectors, and two GRPO-adapted Qwen2.5-7B models, reporting classification ROC-AUC and regression R^2 separately and using dataset-wise ranks for cross-task comparison. Across five seeded evaluation partitions, classical selectors generally achieve higher predictive performance than the tested 7B LLM/RL selectors, including under a pre-specified ~33% feature budget with strict train-only classical fitting, while the 7B selectors retain compact subsets. A cardinality-matched semantic sensitivity experiment shows that, for Zero-shot Qwen-7B, informative feature names improve regression performance over anonymized and shuffled alternatives (+0.1964 and +0.1606 mean R^2), whereas aggregate classification differences are smaller (+0.0159 and +0.0084 ROC-AUC) and dataset-dependent. These results characterize when semantic information benefits LLM-based feature selection and show that classical selectors remain strong baselines for predictive tabular feature selection.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 18 个表格数据集上系统比较经典统计特征选择器、冻结的 Qwen2.5-7B / Llama-3.3-70B 选择器与两个 GRPO 微调的 Qwen2.5-7B 选择器，并检验特征名称语义信息带来的影响，发现经典方法在预测性能上普遍更强。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在特征预算下选择输入子集，并用 GRPO 训练 LLM 选择器」以及语义名称敏感性的诊断，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据/token 的筛选与预算约束下的选择策略提供借鉴线索，需核查奖励设计与语义先验的实际作用。
